This is an actual reanalysis of neurophysiological data, not a citation-only mention, and the task context was also used to define the analyzed behavioral epochs. The dataset was used to support and generalize findings from the authors’ own experiments, so the primary reuse type is CONFIRMATORY; none of the current authors overlap with Grosmark or Buzsáki.

quotes.q: To further investigate synchronous ensembles across different datasets, we analyzed publicly available hippocampal recordings ‘hc-11’ from the CRCNS repository ( Grosmark and Buzsáki, 2016 ; Grosmark et al., 2016 ), where rats navigated novel mazes for water rewards (see Method).

Spikes recorded during the first three minutes of the novel-maze running epochs were used to identify synchronous ensembles and generate jittered control data. Spike counts for both the original and jittered data were calculated using a sliding 25 ms window.

pairs.title: Fast evolutionary turnover and overlapping variances of sex-biased gene expression patterns defy a simple binary sex classification of somatic tissues
pairs.reasoning: The Methods explicitly state that the authors retrieved human single-nucleus RNA-Seq data from the SEA-AD project and downloaded normalized h5ad files from CZ CELLxGENE, then selected control individuals and analyzed cell types in MTG and DLPFC. This is direct reuse of transcriptomic data; the paper does not indicate that it obtained or analyzed electrophysiological recordings, morphology, or behavior. The authors applied a new sex-biased-expression analysis to the existing data, making NOVEL_ANALYSIS the best primary-use category.

quotes.q: The human single-nucleus RNA-Seq data were retrieved from the SEA-AD project (Gabitto et al., 2024). ‘h5ad’ format files, including the normalized read counts using a log transformation of pseudocounts per 10,000 reads, ln(CPTT+1), were downloaded from CZ CELLxGENE (Abdulla et al., 2023; Megill et al., 2021).

pairs.title: Modeling and simulation of neocortical micro- and mesocircuitry (Part I, anatomy)
pairs.reasoning: The Methods explicitly state that the authors analyzed a named MICrONS release and used its synapse table to count connected neuron pairs, which is direct data reuse rather than a citation-only mention. The reused material is EM-derived cell metadata and synaptic-connectivity information, not two-photon activity recordings, so it is classified as other. It was used to validate and compare against the paper's computational anatomical model, making SIMULATION the best reuse type; the MICrONS source group is distinct from this paper's authors.

quotes.q: We analyzed the ‘minnie65_public_v117’ release of the MICrONS data ( https://www.microns-explorer.org/cortical-mm3 ). We restricted the analysis to neurons where the proofreading status was listed as ‘clean’ or ‘extended’.
In that group, 154 pairs were within 100 µm. Of those, 13 were connected according to the ‘synapses_pni_2’ table of the data release.

We then considered neurons where the type of the ‘allen soma coarse cell class model’ was listed as ‘5 P_IT’, ‘5 P_PT’ or ‘5 P_NP’, resulting in 37 neurons. In that group, 154 pairs were within 100 µm. Of those, 13 were connected according to the ‘synapses_pni_2’ table of the data release.
